name: Montenegro

findings.summary: Crnogorski Telekom signed a five-year EUR 12.5m agreement with Ericsson Nikola Tesla to maintain and modernise its whole mobile radio network and introduce 5G nationwide; the partnership was extended at MWC in March 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) is the RAN vendor, so pole third. All three sources are the vendor's own releases, so not corroborated; single-issuer S1 permits medium. Core-network vendor not stated. EUR 12.5m not converted (no source-date rate applied). Crnogorski Telekom is a Magyar Telekom/Deutsche Telekom subsidiary per general knowledge, not verified in opened sources.

findings.controller: 4iG International Digital Infrastructure Zrt. (4iG Group, Hungary)
findings.summary: Montenegro's government selected Hungary's 4iG Group to negotiate design and operation of a Tier III state data centre under a July 2025 Hungary-Montenegro cooperation agreement; costs and financing were still to be defined by a working group.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: 4iG states the government decision to negotiate is not a contractual commitment; no data-centre contract seen as of October 2026. Pole third because 4iG IDI is to operate the facility; ultimate ownership (state vs 4iG) not stated. DCD and IntelliNews both relay 4iG's announcement, so not coded as independent corroboration; single S1 issuer permits medium.

findings.controller: 4iG Informatika Zrt. (4iG IT, Hungary) as system integrator; equipment vendors not named
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Public Works of Montenegro (for law enforcement and border police)
findings.summary: 4iG IT signed a definitive contract with Montenegro's Ministry of Public Works for a EUR 54.25m law-enforcement technology programme: IT and telecom system integration, equipment supply and installation, training and ongoing support for police and border police.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: 4iG is the integrator, and the spec assigns IT equipment to its vendor, which no source names; ongoing support may give 4iG access (then third), so a reviewer may recode. IntelliNews covers only the March selection, not the October signing, so the signed contract rests on 4iG's own S1 statements. EUR 54.25m is the government-set budget, not converted. Whether it includes video surveillance or AI analytics is not stated.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Interior of Montenegro
findings.summary: Presight and Montenegro's Interior Ministry signed an MoU for a long-term framework to build an AI-enabled Smart Nation platform unifying real-time traffic, public-safety, environmental and emergency-response data, during the Prime Minister's visit to Abu Dhabi.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 non-binding MoU; value undisclosed. Presight is a UAE (G42-group) AI firm, so pole third. Month inferred from the 15 May 2026 publication date; signing date not stated. 'Public safety' and 'situational awareness' suggest possible surveillance use, not confirmed. WAM page fetched but returned no article text, so marked unopened. No S1/S2 source opened.
